edges.description: Impaired gap junction communication disrupts calcium signaling and intercellular coordination required for normal keratinocyte differentiation.
Connexin 26 dysfunction in the inner ear disrupts potassium recycling and the endocochlear potential required for hearing.
Chronic aberrant keratinization leads to formation of fibrous constricting bands around digits that progressively tighten and may cause autoamputation.
Impaired connexin 26-mediated keratinocyte differentiation produces diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis.
Aberrant epidermal keratinization on the palms and soles manifests in the characteristic honeycomb hyperkeratotic pattern.
Disordered acral keratinocyte differentiation produces starfish-shaped keratotic plaques over dorsal acral surfaces.
Focal hyperkeratotic thickening over the dorsal interphalangeal joints results from abnormal acral epidermal differentiation.
Nuclear interference with keratinocyte differentiation leads to defective cornification and formation of constricting bands.
Intranuclear accumulation of mutant loricrin disrupts late terminal differentiation of palmoplantar keratinocytes, causing diffuse keratoderma.
Defective late epidermal differentiation from mutant loricrin produces honeycomb palmoplantar hyperkeratosis.
Impaired cornified cell envelope formation and nuclear interference across the generalized epidermis cause ichthyosiform scaling.
Progressive circumferential constriction of the digits compromises distal tissue viability, resulting in clinical pseudoainhum and spontaneous autoamputation.
Impaired cochlear connexin 26 gap-junction function causes sensorineural hearing impairment in classic Vohwinkel syndrome.

nodes.description: Recurrent insertion mutation causing frameshift after codon 231, producing an abnormal C-terminal peptide that mislocalizes to the nucleus.

In the classic GJB2-associated subtype, defective gap junction signaling leads to hyperproliferation and abnormal keratinization of palmoplantar epidermis, resulting in the characteristic thickened honeycomb-patterned skin. This connexin branch is distinct from the LOR-associated mutant loricrin nuclear-accumulation mechanism.

nodes.description: Connexin 26 is essential for potassium recycling in the cochlea. Its dysfunction disrupts the endocochlear potential required for auditory transduction, causing sensorineural hearing loss. This phenotype is specific to GJB2 mutations and is absent in the loricrin-associated variant.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in the connexin26 (Cx26) gene (GJB2) at 13q11-q13 are a major cause of autosomal recessive hearing loss (DFNB1), but have also been reported in autosomal dominant deafness (DFNA3).

nodes.description: Missense mutation (c.196G>C) causing substitution of aspartate to histidine at position 66 in the first extracellular domain. Most common mutation in classic Vohwinkel syndrome.

Fibrous bands encircle digits (pseudoainhum), progressively constricting and potentially leading to spontaneous amputation. The pathogenesis involves aberrant keratinization and tissue remodeling secondary to keratinocyte dysfunction, but the upstream mechanism differs by subtype: GJB2 gap-junction dysfunction in classic Vohwinkel syndrome and mutant loricrin nuclear accumulation in the ichthyotic variant.

evidence.reference_title: A missense mutation in connexin26, D66H, causes mutilating keratoderma with sensorineural deafness (Vohwinkel's syndrome) in three unrelated families.
evidence.snippet: All 10 affected members were heterozygous for a non-conservative mutation, D66H, in Cx26. The same mutation was found subsequently in affected individuals from two unrelated Spanish and Italian pedigrees segregating VS, suggesting that D66H in Cx26 is a common mutation in classical VS.

evidence.reference_title: Vohwinkel Syndrome secondary to missense mutation D66H in GJB2 gene (connexin 26) can include epileptic manifestations.
evidence.snippet: Genetic study showed a nucleotide change (c.196G>C) in exon 1 of GJB2 gene, producing a missense mutation, D66H.

nodes.description: Mutations in GJB2 disrupt connexin 26 function, impairing gap junction-mediated intercellular communication in the epidermis and cochlea. The D66H mutation occurs at a highly conserved residue in the first extracellular domain and may interfere with connexon assembly, docking, or gating properties. This leads to defective ion homeostasis and impaired cellular coordination during differentiation.

evidence.reference_title: A missense mutation in connexin26, D66H, causes mutilating keratoderma with sensorineural deafness (Vohwinkel's syndrome) in three unrelated families.
evidence.snippet: This mutation occurs at a highly conserved residue in the first extracellular domain of the Cx26 molecule, and may exert its effects by interfering with assembly into connexons, docking with adjacent cells or gating properties of the gap junction.

nodes.description: In the ichthyotic variant, mutant loricrin is mislocalized to the nuclei of granular layer keratinocytes and fails to incorporate into the cornified cell envelope. The frameshift mutation creates an abnormal C-terminal peptide containing nuclear localization signals, causing aberrant nuclear translocation and interference with late stages of epidermal differentiation.
